kid.question: What does King Jehoiakim do with the scroll as it is read?

options.text: Cuts it and burns it
Seals it and stores it
Copies it and shares it
Signs it and returns it

kid.explanation: The king cuts the scroll with a penknife and throws it into the fire until it is consumed.

kid.question: What do Elnathan, Delaiah, and Gemariah ask the king?

options.text: To stop reading the scroll
To send the scroll abroad
To stop burning the scroll
To give the scroll back

kid.explanation: The three officials plead with the king not to burn the scroll, but he does not listen.

kid.question: Why are Baruch and Jeremiah not seized?

options.text: The guards have joined them
The king has pardoned them
The priests have released them
The Lord has hidden them

kid.explanation: The king orders their arrest, but the text says the Lord hid them.

kid.question: What does God tell Jeremiah after the scroll burns?

options.text: Send the ashes to Babylon
Write the earlier words again
Bring the king a payment
Wait for a different message

kid.explanation: God tells Jeremiah to take another scroll and write all the former words.

kid.question: What request does Zedekiah send to Jeremiah?

options.text: Pray to God for us
Bring the scroll to us
Find a priest for us
Ask Egypt to help us

kid.explanation: Zedekiah sends messengers asking Jeremiah to pray to the Lord for them.

kid.question: Why do the Chaldeans temporarily leave Jerusalem?

options.text: They learn Judah's king has surrendered
They receive the silver they demanded
They hear their homeland is under attack
They hear Pharaoh's army has come

kid.explanation: News of Pharaoh's army causes the besieging Chaldeans to depart for a time.

kid.question: What does God say will happen after Egypt's army goes home?

options.text: The Egyptians will return and rebuild Jerusalem
The Chaldeans will return and burn Jerusalem
The Judeans will follow and capture Babylon
The priests will leave and settle in Egypt

kid.explanation: God says Pharaoh's army will return to Egypt and the Chaldeans will come again, take the city, and burn it.

kid.question: What does the gate officer accuse Jeremiah of doing?

options.text: Stealing silver from the temple
Hiding soldiers in his house
Going over to the Chaldeans
Sending prisoners back to Egypt

kid.explanation: Irijah accuses Jeremiah of defecting to the Chaldeans; Jeremiah says the accusation is false.

kid.question: What is Jeremiah given each day in the prison court?

options.text: A bowl of olives
A basket of grapes
A portion of fish
A piece of bread

kid.explanation: The king orders a daily piece of bread from the bakers' street until the city's bread is gone.

kid.question: What does Jeremiah sink into in the dungeon?

options.text: Water from a spring
Mud at the bottom
Sand beneath the steps
Grain from a storehouse

kid.explanation: The dungeon has no water but does contain mire, into which Jeremiah sinks.

high-school.question: How do the king and three named officials respond differently to the scroll?

options.text: He preserves it while they demand its destruction
He fears it while they deny that Jeremiah dictated it
He burns it while they plead for him to stop
He rereads it while they hide it from his servants

high-school.explanation: The king burns the scroll despite Elnathan, Delaiah, and Gemariah asking him not to do so.

high-school.question: How is the effort to silence the messengers and their message answered?

options.text: God hides the messengers and orders the words rewritten
God removes the messengers and withdraws the warning
The king releases the messengers and orders a public apology
The officials capture the messengers and restore the original scroll

high-school.explanation: The arrest order fails because God hides them; the Lord then directs Jeremiah to write the former words on another roll.

high-school.question: What part of the message explains the king's hostility?

options.text: The proposal that Egypt will collect Judah's taxes
The demand that Baruch become the next ruler
The instruction that priests must leave the temple
The prediction that Babylon will devastate the land

high-school.explanation: The oracle quotes the king's objection to the prediction of Babylon's destruction of the land and announces judgment on him.

high-school.question: What is the result of replacing the burned scroll?

options.text: The former words are shortened and their warning softened
The former words are restored and similar words added
The king's objections replace the earlier prophetic message
The original warning is preserved without further words

high-school.explanation: Baruch writes all the words of the burned book from Jeremiah's dictation, with many like words added.

high-school.question: What inconsistency marks Zedekiah's request for prayer?

options.text: He seeks royal protection after surrendering his authority
He asks Jeremiah to pray after appointing him temple priest
He seeks prophetic intercession without heeding God's words
He asks for a message after forbidding anyone to speak

high-school.explanation: The narrative says king, servants, and people do not heed God's words, yet Zedekiah asks Jeremiah to pray for them.

high-school.question: Why is the temporary relief from siege an unreliable basis for confidence?

options.text: God says Egypt will leave and Babylon will resume the attack
God says Egypt has already taken permanent control of Judah
God says Babylon's army has surrendered to Judah's remaining soldiers
God says Jerusalem must relocate its people before Egypt returns

high-school.explanation: God warns against assuming the Chaldeans are gone for good; Egypt will withdraw and the Chaldeans will return.

high-school.question: What leads to Jeremiah's imprisonment in Jonathan's house?

options.text: The prophet admits that he has sold military secrets to Babylon
The king condemns him for refusing to pray for the people
The priests discover that he has removed the temple's scrolls
An officer rejects his denial of an accusation of desertion

high-school.explanation: Irijah accuses Jeremiah of defecting, refuses his denial, and brings him to angry officials who beat and imprison him.

high-school.question: How does Jeremiah combine prophetic speech with a personal request?

options.text: He withdraws the warning and asks to become a royal counselor
He repeats the warning and asks not to return to the deadly prison
He offers a new victory promise and asks for a larger daily payment
He refuses to answer and asks to be sent to the Egyptian army

high-school.explanation: Jeremiah tells the king he will be delivered to Babylon and then petitions not to return to Jonathan's house lest he die.

high-school.question: Why do the officials call for Jeremiah's death?

options.text: They regard his surrender message as weakening military resolve
They believe his temple message requires increased military taxes
They accuse him of ordering soldiers to attack the palace
They say his message promises victory only to foreign merchants

high-school.explanation: Jeremiah says those who go to the Chaldeans will live; the officials complain that his words weaken the soldiers and people.

high-school.question: How does Zedekiah respond to the officials' demand?

options.text: He orders Jeremiah released from their custody
He yields control of Jeremiah to them
He directs them to repeat Jeremiah's message
He sends Jeremiah to negotiate with Babylon

high-school.explanation: Zedekiah says Jeremiah is in their hand and claims he cannot act against them; they put Jeremiah in the mire-filled dungeon.

expert.question: Which sequence describes Jehoiakim's treatment of the scroll in Jeremiah 36:22-26?

options.text: The king destroys the text before any reader has brought it into his presence
The king destroys the text after hearing it and rejects pleas to preserve it
The king preserves the text but prevents his servants from hearing its contents
The king revises the text because the three officials dispute its original wording

expert.explanation: The king burns successive portions as they are read and ignores the named officials who plead against burning it.

expert.question: How does the renewed writing reverse the purpose of destroying the scroll?

options.text: The warning survives as a shorter record that accepts the king's objections
The warning becomes a private document stripped of its claims about Babylon
The warning is replaced by a record of the king's successful defense of Judah
The warning survives in full and expands despite the attempt to remove it

expert.explanation: The replacement contains all the former words and many similar words, frustrating the attempted suppression.

expert.question: How does the judgment address both royal succession and personal honor?

options.text: It denies an enthroned successor and announces exposure of the king's corpse
It guarantees an enthroned successor but removes the king's ceremonial clothing
It transfers succession to Baruch and promises the king an honorable burial
It transfers succession to Egypt while preserving the king's public reputation

expert.explanation: The oracle says he will have none to sit on David's throne and his body will be exposed to heat and frost.

expert.question: What does the narrative distinguish in describing the king's approach to Jeremiah?

options.text: Requesting intercession from acknowledging the existence of a prophet
Seeking royal appointment from receiving authority through a foreign ruler
Requesting intercession from heeding the divine word
Seeking military assistance from recognizing Egypt as a neighboring kingdom

expert.explanation: The king's request for prayer is set against the explicit statement that he, servants, and people did not heed God's words.

expert.question: What function does the image of wounded Chaldeans rising from their tents serve?

options.text: It reveals the secret plan by which Judah's soldiers will defeat the siege
It limits the warning to an enemy force that has already recovered its strength
It removes reliance on military appearances as a way to dismiss the warning
It makes the city's burning depend on Egypt's cooperation with Babylon

expert.explanation: Even a hypothetical remnant of wounded Chaldeans would burn the city, underscoring the certainty of the announced judgment.

expert.question: How does Jeremiah's later appeal challenge the basis of his detention?

options.text: He accepts desertion and requests the legal treatment promised to foreign soldiers
He denies desertion and contrasts his warning with the other prophets' failed assurances
He denies prophetic authority and blames the warning on the officers who arrested him
He accepts prophetic error and asks the king to approve a corrected victory message

expert.explanation: Jeremiah denies Irijah's accusation, later asks what offense merits prison, and challenges the prophets who said Babylon would not come.

expert.question: What limit remains on the relief Jeremiah receives from the king?

options.text: Confinement continues and daily bread lasts only while the city has bread
Confinement ends but daily bread must be collected from the Babylonian camp
The king promises freedom once Jeremiah changes his message about the siege
The king sends him home but requires repayment for the bread already supplied

expert.explanation: Zedekiah moves him to the prison court and orders bread until the city's supply is spent; Jeremiah remains confined.

expert.question: What competing definitions of the people's welfare produce the conflict?

options.text: Prophetic survival through battle conflicts with officials' insistence on immediate surrender
Prophetic safety through emigration conflicts with officials' desire to reopen temple worship
Prophetic safety through Egyptian tribute conflicts with officials' defense of Babylonian rule
Prophetic survival through surrender conflicts with officials' insistence on military morale

expert.explanation: Jeremiah offers life to those going out to the Chaldeans, while the officials regard the message as weakening defenders and seeking harm.

expert.question: How does the king's disclaimer translate into action against the prophet?

options.text: Claimed inability to oppose Babylon leads him to release Jeremiah as an envoy
Claimed inability to feed the city leads him to appoint Jeremiah over its stores
Claimed inability to oppose the officials permits their confinement of Jeremiah
Claimed inability to command the priests permits Jeremiah to take charge of worship

expert.explanation: Zedekiah says he cannot act against the officials and gives Jeremiah into their hand; they lower him into the dungeon.

expert.question: What narrative movement closes the day's reading after Jeremiah is lowered into mire?

options.text: News of the imprisonment moves a royal servant to approach the king
News of the imprisonment moves Babylon's commander to release the prisoners
The king publicly confesses his error and orders immediate surrender to Babylon
The princes retract their charge and offer to defend Jeremiah's prophetic message

expert.explanation: Ebed-melech hears of the dungeon and goes out to speak to the king. The rescue itself is beyond this daily slice.
